scope_plain: Every Missouri voter. This is the only statewide executive office on Missouri's 2026 ballot; governor, lieutenant governor, attorney general, secretary of state and treasurer are elected in 2028, and neither U.S. Senate seat is up this year.
office_explainer: The state's independent watchdog. Audits state agencies, counties and local governments for waste, fraud and legal compliance.
why_it_matters: The auditor decides which governments get audited and publishes the findings. The office also writes the fiscal notes voters see on ballot measures, so it shapes what you read about every amendment's cost. Four-year term.

candidates.name: Scott Fitzpatrick
candidates.background: State auditor since January 2023. Before that, state treasurer (2019 to 2023) and a state representative from Shell Knob who became 'the youngest Chairman of the Budget committee in Missouri history.' Grew up on Table Rock Lake; owns a boat-dock business that now employs about 70 people. Won the August 4 Republican primary with 85.5%.

own_words.text: "Where waste, fraud, and abuse occur, I will find it and root it out."
"As Auditor, I will lead a comprehensive audit of any local government," and review school district administrative costs and salaries.
On the state budget squeeze: the auditor's role is to "bring a level of seriousness … that I think has not existed."

candidates.name: Quentin Wilson
candidates.background: Kirkwood resident (St. Louis County). Director of the Missouri Department of Revenue starting in 1998, then cabinet director under Gov. Bob Holden from 2001; also deputy director of Economic Development and state Commissioner of Higher Education. Earlier an aide to three members of Congress. Won the August 4 Democratic primary with 67.9%.

own_words.text: The office should be "a check on unlimited and unaccountable power." "One party cannot police itself."
"Everybody Counts. And Every Dollar Counts." Wants audits that go beyond whether "the books balance": "It is the auditor's job to help people streamline and improve."
Says his agency streamlining work as revenue director "saved taxpayers millions of dollars."

office: Supreme Court of Missouri: retain Judge Paul C. Wilson?
scope_plain: Every Missouri voter. Missouri uses the 'nonpartisan court plan': the governor appoints appellate judges from a commission's list, then voters decide yes or no on keeping them. No Supreme Court judge has lost a retention vote since the plan began in 1940.
office_explainer: Highest state court. Final say on Missouri law. Vote yes to keep the judge, no to remove.
why_it_matters: The seven-member Supreme Court decides challenges to state laws and ballot measures; this year it put Proposition A and Amendment 6 on the ballot and ruled that the 2025 congressional map cannot take effect unless voters approve it, so the 2022 map is used for this year's U.S. House races. A judge who is retained serves another 12 years. The Judicial Performance Review Committee's majority recommends retaining Judge Wilson; it publishes no vote count.

candidates.name: Paul C. Wilson
candidates.background: On the Supreme Court since December 2012 (appointed by Gov. Jay Nixon); chief justice July 2021 to June 2023. Earlier a circuit judge in Cole County (19th Circuit), an assistant Missouri attorney general, and a lawyer at Sullivan & Cromwell and a Jefferson City firm. Drury College; University of Missouri law, cum laude. Retained by voters in 2014.

evaluations.vote_note: The committee publishes only its majority recommendation, not a vote count.
evaluations.survey_note: Missouri's lawyer survey uses 1-to-5 ratings on many questions, with no single yes-or-no question, so there is no one number to show. The full results are on the judge's page.

office: Missouri Court of Appeals, Eastern District: retain Judge Virginia W. Lay?
district: Eastern District (St. Louis City and County and 23 other eastern counties)
scope_plain: Voters in the Eastern District only, which includes all of St. Louis County and the City of St. Louis. Each judge gets a separate yes/no question.
office_explainer: Mid-level appeals court for eastern Missouri. Reviews trial court decisions. Vote yes to keep the judge, no to remove.
why_it_matters: Most appeals in Missouri end here; the Supreme Court takes only a few cases a year. A judge retained serves 12 more years. Newly appointed judges face their first retention vote at the first general election after a year on the bench. The Judicial Performance Review Committee's majority recommends retaining Judge Lay; it publishes no vote count.

Earlier an assistant circuit attorney in St. Louis, assistant prosecutor in Jackson County, assistant attorney general, and in private practice in employment and municipal law. Washington University law. First retention vote.
